fields.rationale: Authorities are grouped by the structural type of the issuing body: a board dedicated solely to that profession; a board shared across two or more distinct professions; a state health department or public-health agency; a general professional licensing or consumer-protection agency spanning many fields; a labor/industry/commerce department; or another executive agency that fits none of the above.

Boards are bucketed by the type of institution that regulates the profession: a board dedicated solely to that profession, a board shared with closely related professions, a broader medical or healing-arts board that absorbs smaller health professions, a state health department, a general professional-licensing or financial-regulation agency, or a labor/commerce/consumer-affairs department.

Rows are grouped by the functional type of the umbrella department—health, consumer protection, commerce, dedicated professional licensing, labor, secretary of state, education, or a residual catch-all—regardless of the specific profession regulated.

Each raw value names a type of authority that must accredit the applicant's program; the buckets distinguish who holds that authority — a dedicated national accreditor for that field, a general regional/institutional accreditor, an explicit federal reference, the licensing board itself, a state-level agency, or a federal workforce/apprenticeship body.

Each value was bucketed by the dominant gate that triggers recognition: whether the primary requirement is that the other state's standards are substantially equivalent; that the applicant has practiced for a minimum number of years; that a formal interstate compact pathway exists; that a specific exam or national certification was passed; that both states must have a bilateral reciprocity agreement; that the applicant merely holds a license and pays a fee; or that a demanding multi-factor review (education + exam + experience + character + discipline checks) governs.
